findings.title: Sorting by formatted string instead of numeric amount
findings.description: The sort key is format_money(kv[1]), which formats cents into a display string (e.g. '$9.99'). Sorting these strings lexicographically does not produce a numeric ordering (e.g. '$100.00' sorts before '$20.00' as strings), so top_categories can return categories that are not actually the biggest spenders. The sort should use the raw integer cents value, not the formatted string.

findings.title: Alphabetical tie-break not implemented
findings.description: The docstring claims ties are broken alphabetically, but the sort key only uses format_money(kv[1]); the category name is never included in the sort key, so tied categories retain arbitrary/insertion order from dict.items() rather than being ordered alphabetically.

findings.title: No handling of n <= 0 or empty spend
findings.description: top_categories does not validate n; passing n=0 or a negative n silently returns an empty or oddly-sliced list rather than raising a clear error, which could mask caller bugs.

findings.title: No tests added for top_categories
findings.description: The diff introduces a new public function with non-trivial sorting/formatting/tie-break behavior but adds no unit tests to verify ordering, truncation to n, tie-break behavior, or formatting output, so the numeric-vs-string sort bug above would not be caught.
